business_scope.primary_industry_name: Open-Market Brokerage of Solid-State Drives and Server Processors

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Agreement on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed 30 November 2007 and in force from 20 August 2010, subject to its scope and applicable investor nationality requirements
France-China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 26 November 2013 and in force from 28 December 2015
Applicable France-EU treaties and directly applicable European Union company, customs, VAT, sanctions and anti-money-laundering legislation
Any additional France bilateral investment treaty or double-tax treaty depends on the nationality and tax residence of the shareholder, beneficial owner and financing parties
The EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment is not in force and should not be treated as an operative treaty protection

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT rules are contained in the French Monetary and Financial Code, including Articles L.561-2, L.561-4-1, L.561-5, L.561-6, L.561-10, L.561-15 and L.561-32. Beneficial-owner identification and filing obligations are principally governed by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and Articles R.561-55 to R.561-63 of the Monetary and Financial Code. The beneficial-owner filing framework was implemented and supplemented by Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 and subsequent amendments. Corporate formation and beneficial-owner filings are submitted through the French National Business Register and the INPI single-window system. Access to beneficial-owner data is restricted following Court of Justice of the European Union judgment C-37/20 and related French implementing measures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation or current registry extract, apostilled or legalized and accompanied by a certified French translation where required; a 90-day issuance period is a practical acceptance standard, not a universal statutory expiry rule
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry or company authority in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country is party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the issuing authority, the competent French consular post and any required intermediate authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate shareholder articles of association and current constitutional documents, apostilled or legalized where requested by the filing agent or authority; a 90-day document date is a practical freshness standard
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notary or competent public authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate or declaration of incumbency, directors and authorized signatories, with authority to establish the French SARL and execute powers of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry, notary, corporate secretary or other legally recognized authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholder resolution approving incorporation, capital subscription, appointment of the manager and execution of the French incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder or its competent governing body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required by the receiving authority or institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the French incorporation representative, with signature certification and French translation where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign shareholder, beneficial owner or authorized representative

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document for each manager, direct individual shareholder and identified beneficial owner; notarized copy only where required by the filing agent, bank or foreign issuing practice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or identity-document authority in the country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization only where specifically required; otherwise certified copy accepted subject to French KYC procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-owner ownership and control chart tracing ownership through every intermediate entity to the natural persons exercising ownership or control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Prepared by the applicant and supported by registry evidence and constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Supporting foreign public documents require Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; the chart itself is generally not independently legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence for treaty, banking or substance review, where requested
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax authority in the relevant shareholder or beneficial-owner jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required by the receiving institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, banks, corporate service providers and regulated professionals should screen all shareholders, managers, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, counterparties and relevant payment parties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union sanctions, French national sanctions and applicable OFAC lists. PEP, family-member and close-associate screening is mandatory for obliged entities under French AML rules, with enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification and enhanced transaction monitoring where applicable. Screening should cover aliases, transliterations, former names, adverse media, export-control restrictions, proliferation-financing indicators, dual-use technology exposure and high-risk jurisdictions. OFAC is not generally binding on a non-US French entity, but becomes commercially relevant for US persons, US-dollar clearing, US-origin technology, US banks or contractual sanctions undertakings.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration data recorded in the Registre national des entreprises; the official portal is formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a French SARL must be stated in the incorporation documents and followed by or immediately preceded by the designation Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL and the stated share capital. French company names may use Latin characters and foreign-language terms, but the name must not be misleading, unlawful, contrary to public order or confusingly similar to a protected company name, trade name, trademark or domain name. French accents and spelling should be preserved in the registered name. A translated or transliterated trading name does not replace the legally registered French company name. Separate trademark, domain-name and trade-name searches are required because company-name registration does not create universal trademark protection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation period of 30 days for a SARL. A proposed name may be checked through INPI, Infogreffe, trademark databases and domain registries, but legal protection generally arises from valid use, registration and applicable intellectual-property rights rather than from a universal reservation certificate. If the INPI single window or the competent registry rejects the proposed name, obtain the electronic rejection notice and stated legal basis, correct the name or supporting documents, and resubmit within the prescribed correction period. For an administrative decision that remains disputed, file a reasoned administrative challenge with the competent authority and, where appropriate, an administrative appeal before the competent administrative court within the applicable time limit stated in the decision. If the issue concerns a trademark, company name or unfair competition claim, use the appropriate civil or commercial court and, for trademark matters, the relevant INPI opposition or cancellation procedure. A new non-conflicting name is usually faster and less costly than litigating a preventable similarity objection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SARL must have a registered office in France under the French Commercial Code, including Articles L.123-11 and following. Domiciliation through an authorized domiciliation company is generally permissible if the provider is legally authorized and the contractual and premises requirements are satisfied. A manager may, subject to statutory conditions, use a home address for a limited period. For wholesale SSDs and server processors, a virtual office may satisfy the registered-office requirement but does not by itself establish operational substance. The company should maintain accessible accounting and corporate records, genuine management activity, supplier and customer documentation, customs and VAT evidence, inventory or logistics arrangements, product traceability, sanctions and export-control procedures, and a bankable commercial rationale. A warehouse, fulfillment provider or third-party logistics location may be used if properly documented; ownership of inventory and import responsibilities must be clearly allocated.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official French statistical probability is published for unannounced inspections of newly incorporated SARLs. For this medium-risk wholesale semiconductor activity, an operational planning estimate is 5-15% during an ordinary first three-year period, increasing materially if there are customs anomalies, unexplained intra-group payments, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctions or export-control concerns, VAT irregularities, inconsistent beneficial-owner information, dormant-company indicators or a regulated-bank escalation. This is a risk estimate only and not a statutory probability.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI single window and relevant French registration authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative tariffs, converted approximately from euros; tariffs may change

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial-owner filing and related register formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI single window and competent register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official filing tariff where charged; otherwise filing-agent market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal notice publication for formation of the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government-regulated or capped publication tariff based on department and notice length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translations of foreign corporate documents, identity documents and ownership records

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official legalization charges plus courier and document-handling market costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French corporate, UBO and AML pre-incorporation due-diligence review, including ownership-chain analysis and sanctions screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional market benchmark; not generally subject to a mandatory statutory fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate records, incorporation resolutions, manager appointment documents and filing powers of attorney

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation and corporate governance); Article L.210-2 (subscription and payment of capital); Articles R.223-1 to R.223-11 (RCS registration formalities); Article L.123-1 et seq. and implementing regulations for the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the registered office department; filings are transmitted through the INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) using the official dematerialized form Cerfa No. 11407 (M0).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital is imposed for a SARL (may be set at EUR 1). Cash contributions must be paid up to at least one-fifth (20%) at subscription; the remaining balance must be released within five years. Capital deposits must be held on a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts until incorporation is completed, and a certificate of deposit is required for the RCS filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved by the original shareholders of the Company: (1) The share capital of EUR [amount] is fully subscribed and each cash contribution has been paid up in an amount of at least one-fifth, deposited in a blocked bank account in accordance with Articles L.223-7 and L.210-2 of the French Commercial Code. (2) The Draft Articles of Association are approved and adopted as the sole constitutive instrument. (3) The registered office is fixed at [address] in the jurisdiction of [city], France. (4) Mr/Ms [full name] is appointed Gérant (Manager) with full power to represent the Company in all wholesale trading, brokerage and related activities. (5) The Gérant is authorized to publish the legal notice, complete all registrations and carry out all formalities before the competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance and AML/KYC pre-validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Data portal (data.inpi.fr) and registered professional intermediaries; appointed bank for KYC screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the chosen company name on data.inpi.fr and obtain a name availability statement; collect identity proofs and beneficial ownership declarations for all shareholders and managers; verify there is no sectoral prohibition for wholesale electronic-component brokerage; fix the corporate object as 'brokerage and wholesale of solid-state drives and server processors'.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity card of all shareholders and managers
Proof of residential address dated less than three months
Professional curriculum vitae or background statement for the proposed Gérant
AML/KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is not available or KYC documentation is incomplete, select a corrected name and amend the beneficial-ownership declaration; resubmit only after clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and legal counsel; optional notary (notaire) if an in-kind contribution of immovable property or a regulated asset is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French, including share capital amount and classes, shareholder quotas, management powers, corporate purpose, duration, registered office address, dispute resolution, and audit thresholds. All pages must be initialed and the document signed by all shareholders; non-cash contributions must be described and valued in an annex if present.
required_dossiers: Draft and final Articles of Association
Identity documents of shareholders and manager
Statement of contribution and valuation annex if in-kind contributions exist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a notary queries statutory inconsistencies, execute an amending document by unanimous shareholders' consent and re-initial all pages before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital deposit and blocked account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company account in the name of the SARL in formation, transfer the full subscribed capital into it, and obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage des fonds). At least 20% of cash contributions must be available immediately; the remaining installments are governed by the statutory five-year schedule.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of contributing shareholders
Draft Articles of Association
Completed bank opening forms and Certificate of subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires more detailed KYC or a recalculation of capital, correct the shareholder contribution schedule and obtain a revised attestation before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved French legal gazette (Journal d'annonces légales, JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare an 'Avis de constitution' containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, address, corporate purpose, manager identity, and registration information; publish the notice in an authorized JAL and obtain the publisher's attestation (attestation de parution) required for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association
Certificate of deposit of capital
Identity details of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal gazette rejects the wording for containing inaccuracies, correct the avis and re-publish; the corrected attestation must be attached to the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Dematerialized filing with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique portal, complete the M0 application for SARL incorporation, upload the statuts, certificate of capital deposit, legal notice attestation, identity documents, beneficial ownership declaration, and pay the official filing fees online. The portal sends the file to the competent Registry of the Commercial Court and other administrations.
required_dossiers: Cerfa M0 application form completed online
Signed Articles of Association
Blocked account certificate (attestation de blocage)
Legal publication attestation (attestation de parution)
Passport copies and address proofs
Beneficial owner declaration and residence certificate for each shareholder if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique sends an incompleteness query, supplement the dossier within 15 days by uploading the missing PDFs; retain the electronic acknowledgment of conclusive filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the registered office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the submitted file, the registry assigns a RCS number, SIREN and SIRET numbers, an APE code corresponding to the main activity, and issues the official 'extrait Kbis' confirming the legal existence and powers of the company.
required_dossiers: Complete M0 filing packet transmitted by the Guichet Unique
Certificate of capital deposit
Legal notice publication attestation
Original signed Articles of Association where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry asks for clarification on the corporate purpose or manager powers, provide an explanatory legal memo or a shareholders' rectification resolution and re-submit through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, VAT, social and beneficial owner notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises), URSSAF, INSEE, and Infogreffe/TEI platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the French VAT number using form 3550 once the Kbis is obtained, register the beneficial owner information on the TEI (Transfert Électronique d'Informations) platform if not already embedded, verify SIRET allocation, and notify URSSAF of the employer status before first hiring activity.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Form 3550 VAT registration application or online equivalent
Beneficial ownership return (certificat de dépôt) if applicable
Bank account details and signatory mandate
URSSAF registration form if any employees are planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or social registrations are delayed, provide proof of the Kbis and RCS effective date and request an expedited processing request through the DGFiP counter or URSSAF online assurance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) for industry policy; DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités) for labor and occupational safety enforcement; the Préfecture for site-specific physical and environmental approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating license is required for pure brokerage and wholesale of electronic components. If a warehouse or physical stockholding site is established, the operation will be subject to the ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) registration or declaration regime under the French Environmental Code depending on the floor area and storage volumes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité environnementale - Conseil général de l'environnement et du développement durable (CGEDD), in coordination with DREETS and the local Préfecture services for site permitting.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Application of the à la carte EIA scheme: a full environmental impact assessment is not triggered for office-only wholesale/brokerage. Where a storage or distribution warehouse is operated, the project is classified under ICPE nomenclature (e.g., entries 1510, 1511 or 1530) as 'Declarable' or 'Registrable' depending on floor area; a complete EIA is required only if thresholds under Article R.122-2 are exceeded, which is unlikely for a standard wholesale electronics depot.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only activities have no industrial discharge thresholds. For warehousing, sanitary and roof wastewater must comply with municipal pre-treatment standards under Articles R.1331-21 and R.1331-29 of the Environmental Code; stormwater runoff must respect urban discharge levels; no significant VOC or hazardous effluent is expected. Waste handling must comply with waste tracking, storage, and disposal obligations under the Environmental Code, and traded goods must meet French transposition of RoHS/REACH product restrictions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: attestation of compliance with ERP (Établissement Recevant du Public) rules if a public reception area is open; otherwise, employee-only office buildings must comply with labor fire prevention rules and obtain a landlord or DREETS inspection certificate. Structural load inspections are required for high-bay racking in any warehouse. Occupational clearance: preparation of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques (DUER), registration of workstations with the occupational health service, medical surveillance for staff, and a DREETS labor inspection clearance where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); official portal: impots.gouv.fr. Non-resident taxpayers are handled by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) and the Centre des Impôts des Non-Résidents (CINR), 10 Rue du Centre, 93160 Noisy-le-Grand. Corporate formation is effected via the mandatory single electronic window (Guichet unique) operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs clearance and export control are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL through the Guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); the resulting registration in the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) automatically generates the 9-digit SIREN and the SIRET establishment code. Step 2: DGFiP automatically allocates the French intra-Community VAT identification number (FR + 2-digit cryptographic key + 9-digit SIREN) to the registered head office pursuant to Articles 286-I and 286 quater CGI. Step 3: A non-established foreign wholesaler with taxable French supplies (e.g., goods stored in French third-party logistics) must file a 'Demande d'immatriculation d'un assujetti non établi' with the SIEE, attaching constitutional documents, a copy of the trade/business register of the foreign entity, the underlying supply contract, the French EORI number, directors' identification, and a power of attorney. Step 4: A foreign entity without any EU fixed establishment must appoint an accredited tax representative ('représentant fiscal agréé') who is jointly and severally liable for French VAT (Article 289 A CGI) and must post a bank guarantee. Step 5: After VAT registration, the taxpayer must file the DeB/DEB (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens) for intra-EU goods movements and maintain an EORI number issued by DGDDI for customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – A French SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax ('impôt sur les sociétés', IS) under Article 206-1 CGI, taxable on profits derived from businesses operated in France in accordance with the territoriality principle of Article 209-I CGI. The SARL is not fiscally transparent; distributions to shareholders are separately taxed (in France, generally a 30% flat tax for individuals or a withholding tax regime for non-residents). The company may, under strict statutory conditions, elect transient income-tax transparency, but the default classification is entity-level corporate taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (a) Income-tax transparency option under Article 239 bis AA CGI, allowing a small SARL to be taxed at the level of its individual partners ('régime fiscal des sociétés de personnes') for five financial years, renewable, subject to cumulative conditions: at least 50% of the capital held by natural persons, fewer than 50 employees, annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, and exercise of a commercial, industrial, artisanal or liberal activity; (b) French fiscal consolidation ('intégration fiscale') under Article 223 A CGI, available to a French parent holding at least 95% of the shares of each French subsidiary, elected for five years and renewable; (c) VAT grouping election ('assujetti unique') under Article 256 C CGI for closely linked French companies; (d) hybrid mismatch recharacterization under Article 38 bis CGI is automatic under ATAD and not elective. France does not provide a US-style check-the-box regime; entity classification is statutory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – 'Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée' (TVA), governed by Articles 256 to 289 C of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL carrying on wholesale of goods, there is no monetary threshold excluding registration: the company is a taxable person and must obtain a French VAT number from its first transaction, notwithstanding the theoretical micro-business VAT exemption ('franchise en base de TVA', Article 293 B CGI) available up to EUR 101,000 annual turnover for sale of goods and EUR 39,100 for services (2025 thresholds, with upper ceiling of EUR 111,000 / EUR 44,700 after which exemption lapses entirely). For non-established foreign enterprises supplying goods or B2B services into France, registration is compulsory from the first euro of taxable French turnover; the EU-wide distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 for cross-border B2C distance sales does not apply to wholesale B2B supplies. Intra-Community acquisitions by a French VAT-registered SARL require a valid French VAT ID, and no local IT procurement threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory domestic B2B e-invoicing enters into force under Article 289 bis CGI in two phases: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices, and large and medium-sized enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 small and micro-enterprises must issue them. Invoices must use the French normative structured format (Factur-X / EN 16931) and be exchanged through an accredited 'Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire' (PDP) or the national public portal 'FNFE-M' via secure APIs. E-reporting obligations require transmission of transaction data for cross-border supplies of goods and services and for B2C supplies to DGFiP through the same channel. France follows a post-audit continuous-transaction-control model rather than real-time governmental clearance; no digital stamp or real-time fiscal approval is required. Sanctions for non-compliance include graduated fines of EUR 15 per missing or non-compliant invoice and EUR 20 per omitted e-reporting record, subject to annual caps of EUR 15,000 and EUR 20,000 respectively, increased in cases of bad faith.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération à 0% with full right to input VAT recovery) applies under two parallel regimes: (1) Non-EU exports under Article 262-I-1° CGI, for tangible goods dispatched or transported by or on behalf of the seller to a destination outside the European Union, provided the seller is the exporter on the French customs export declaration and the goods physically leave EU customs territory; (2) Intra-Community supplies under Article 262-I-2° CGI, where goods are shipped from France to a taxable customer registered for VAT in another Member State, with the customer's valid intra-Community VAT number quoted and the supplier filing the EC Sales List (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens) and the recapitulative statement under Article 289 B CGI. Offshore services directly linked to exported goods may also be zero-rated in limited cases under Article 259 A CGI and Article 262-I-1°, but pure digital or remote services are taxable at 20% at the customer's place of establishment under the B2B reverse charge (Article 283-2 CGI). For the wholesale of SSDs and server processors, physical export or intra-EU dispatch must be fully evidenced before the zero rate is claimed on the periodic VAT return; in the absence of compliant evidence, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 20%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation – DE) lodged electronically in the DELTA customs system, with the assigned MRN (Movement Reference Number) and the electronic proof of exit transmitted by DGDDI through the European Export Control System (ECS/ARC).

Commercial invoice and packing list reflecting precise quantities, serial numbers, unit values, Incoterms and the buyer's identity; the invoice must state the applicable zero-rating provision (Article 262-I-1° or 262-I-2° CGI).

Transport documentation evidencing exit from EU territory: Bill of Lading (B/L) for sea freight, CMR/consignment note for road freight, or Air Waybill (AWB) for air freight, issued to the foreign buyer or to an authorized customs broker/forwarder.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice proving settlement of the export sale in convertible currency and repatriation of proceeds to the French exporting entity.

For intra-Community supplies: EC Sales List (DEB) and the recapitulative statement of Article 289 B CGI filed with the French statistical/customs authorities, plus documentary proof of transport into the destination Member State and the customer's valid intra-Community VAT number.

EORI number issued by DGDDI and retained in the exporter's register; where applicable, the 'preuve de l'exportation' file must be completed with the customs exit certification before the VAT return deadline.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and tax authorities conduct systematic post-clearance audits of export evidence. There is no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline in French VAT law; the 180-day figure is a conservative internal compliance benchmark reflecting the payment horizon accepted by fiscal auditors for documentary substantiation; a payment outstanding beyond 180 days triggers heightened scrutiny and burden of proof. If the export proof is missing, invalid or forged, the zero-rated supply is recharacterized as taxable at 20% (Article 272 CGI), with immediate VAT recovery. Standard penalties: late-payment interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI), a 40% penalty for bad faith (mauvaise foi) and an 80% penalty for deliberate fraud or 'manœuvres frauduleuses' (Article 1729 CGI). Criminal exposure under Article 1741 CGI reaches EUR 500,000 fine and five years' imprisonment, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and seven years for organized VAT fraud. In MTIC (Missing Trader Intra-Community) cases, the exporter may lose the exemption even where goods physically left France if it knew or should have known of the fraud, with joint and several liability under Article 283-4 CGI. The reassessment window is three years under Article L.168 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales (LPF), extended to six years where a return was omitted or fraudulent (Article L.176 LPF). Recovery is enforced through administrative attachment ('saisie administrative à tiers détenteur') and customs seizure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting under the regulatory oversight of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member state with full currency convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions on the conversion of euros to foreign currency or vice versa. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is freely permitted, subject to standard corporate tax and withholding tax obligations, and no prior administrative authorization is required. Capital repatriation and dividend distributions are equally unrestricted, cross-border payments are processed via the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) and SWIFT rails. The only obligations are reporting and declaration to the Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP) and the customs authority for statistical and tax purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or any government-controlled entity, and no mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency accounts with any licensed credit institution in France or abroad, subject to mandatory declaration of cross-border physical cash movements exceeding EUR 10,000 (under EU Regulation (EC) No 1889/2005) and electronic payment reporting to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. All invoicing and settlement documentation must be retained for at least six years for audit and tax inspection purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with legal constraints. French-registered Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto and Shine, or ACPR-licensed fintechs, can provide fully digital onboarding and core settlement accounts in euros. However, EMIs are generally not licensed to provide foreign exchange hedging derivatives or complex trade finance instruments such as letters of credit, and may not hold funds in segregated escrow with the same creditor protection as full banks. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK-licensed or Asia-Pacific) face substantial legal limitations; they cannot hold French corporate accounts without a branch or passported licence, and French tax authorities will not recognize them for escrow or trade settlement purposes. T1 strategy therefore should pair an EMI for operational agility with a T1 bank for escrow, hedging, and LC issuance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is generally required for first-time corporate account opening at traditional T1 French banks. Remote opening is available at licensed EMIs and select neo-banks, but for a wholesale semiconductor trading entity, a physical interview at the bank branch (or at the entity's registered office with a notaire-certified document package) substantially improves onboarding success. For non-resident directors, a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney is required; however, the ultimate beneficial owner(s) must personally appear for identity verification unless an enhanced video-KYC process has been pre-approved by the bank's compliance committee, which remains case-by-case and non-guaranteed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus: involvement of counterparties, payment intermediaries, or ultimate beneficial owners residing in or transiting through FATF grey-list or non-cooperative tax jurisdictions (e.g., certain CIS, Middle East, or offshore financial centres), triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract (Kbis) with apostille; full shareholder register; detailed CVs and notarized ID copies of all directors and UBOs with tax residency proof (tax certificate or residence certificate); signed sworn affidavit from the compliance officer describing the bona fide commercial relationship; valid import/export licence (where required); complete list of counterparties with their own KYC packs; and underlying supply contracts proving real economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high transaction velocity or large-value wires relative to registered share capital and projected turnover, particularly in high-value electronics components, raising suspicion of unlicensed money services business, trade-based money laundering, or sanctions evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed audited business plan with realistic monthly turnover projections; binding purchase orders and sales contracts with actual prices, quantities, and delivery terms; bank statements of the parent or related entities showing traceable source of funds; proforma invoices from major suppliers (e.g., authorized distributors like Arrow, Ingram Micro, or Avnet); customs declarations (DAU) and logistics documentation proving physical cross-border movement of goods; and an approved internal AML/KYC policy manual with transaction thresholds and monitoring protocols.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control sensitivity of semiconductor products with CPU and SSD capabilities, triggering screening flags if any counterparty, trade lane, or ultimate consignee is denied-party listed, or if goods might be re-exported to military or surveillance end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed Denied Party Screening (DPS) reports from a recognized screening tool (e.g., Dow Jones, LexisNexis, or OFAC tool) showing all counterparties cleared; end-user of end-use declaration certification for advanced-level chips (EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821); Supply chain audit trail from OEM manufacturer to final customer; written CSP (Comprehensive Sanctions Procedure) plan; and a compliance undertaking letter (lettre d'engagement) that the entity will not transact with or re-export to restricted jurisdictions without prior authorization from DG Trésor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident shareholders must be executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer with purpose code 'G302' (EU/EEA statistical purpose code for direct investment in the reporting country) or 'CG01' for capital transactions, depending on the sending bank's mapping to the IMF Balance of Payments Manual (BPM6). The corporate treasury must provide supporting documentation to the receiving French bank, including the shareholders' resolution, share subscription agreement, and a notarized copy of the French entity's Kbis. Wire transfers over EUR 10,000 must be reported to the Banque de France within 20 business days after the transaction (monthly reporting for recurring flows). All funds must be credited to the SARL's capital escrow account before any operational disbursement to comply with French money-laundering rules and to secure the bank's 'customer acceptance' pattern. For immediate liquidity, funds may be transferred via SWIFT as an 'equity contribution in kind' or 'shareholder current account advance', but such advances must be documented with an advance agreement (convention de trésorerie) to avoid deemed dividend treatment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to foreign suppliers and service providers must be executed primarily through SWIFT (MT103/202) for T/T operations and commercial letters of credit (documentary credits, UCP600-compliant) for larger or riskier procurement volumes. The standard clearing rail is SEPA in euros for EU counterparties (hard-coded creditor account with IBAN), and SWIFT for non-EU suppliers in USD, CNY, or HKD. For each outbound disbursement, the French bank requires a supporting commercial invoice, a shipping document (bill of lading or air waybill), and a customs declaration (if physical export from France). Purpose codes for outbound payment should align with BPM6: 'G401' (imports of goods) for inventory restocking, 'G502' (trade credit) for pre-import financing, and 'G306' (direct investment abroad) for funding overseas branches. There is no statutory settlement timeline restriction, but the bank's AML call-back procedures may require a 'purpose of payment' statement for each transfer. Escrowed payment linked to an inspection certificate (SOC or SGS) is the recommended clearing rail for transactions with untested suppliers; the bank may issue a 'sight payment under instruction' confirming the exporter will be paid only after presentation of the pre-issued inspection certificate/quality compliance rating.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward Contracts: OTC forward purchase or sale of EUR against USD, CNY, HKD, or other non-EUR trade currencies for periods of 1 week to 12 months, executable with a licensed French bank subject to ISDA or FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement, no margin requirement for SME clients on covered trades.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): Suitable for currencies with limited onshore liquidity (e.g., low-liquidity Asian or CIS currencies), though for the primary trade currencies (USD, CNY, HKD) deliverable forwards are preferable and cheap; NDFs require separate ISDA-style documentation and a European Market Infrastructure Regulation (EMIR) reporting obligation.

Cross-Currency Swaps: EUR-USD or EUR-CNY cross-currency interest rate swaps, used to hedge both FX and interest-rate exposure on intra-group loans or supplier financing facilities; must be entered into under an approved ISDA 2002 Master Agreement; EMIR centralized clearing exemption available for the SARL as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold.

FX Options (Plain Vanilla): OTC call or put options providing conditional hedging flexibility against contingent tender or procurement outcomes; allowed with bank approval under the same ISDA/FBF documentation architecture.
FX Swaps (Long-term): Net-settlement swap agreements hedging principal conversion for loan servicing or cross-border share subscription efforts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report filed at the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des Formalités
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' annual general meeting must approve the accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; the approved accounts must be filed within 1 month after approval. For a calendar-year SARL, the final deposit date is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL to a court injunction with daily penalty (astreinte), administrative fines, and potential administrative strike-off from the RCS; undistributed profits cannot be lawfully paid if accounts are not approved within the statutory period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' general meeting and recorded shareholder decisions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory register; no direct RCS filing unless accompanied by amendments to bylaws or changes in capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 6 months from fiscal year-end; extension only by court order upon a properly grounded request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene within the legal period invalidates profit appropriation and exposes managers to civil liability; any shareholder may petition the court to designate an agent to convene the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration and balance of corporate income tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year fiscal periods, electronic filing is due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year, with the balance of corporate income tax due on the same date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 5% surcharge on assessed tax plus 0.2% monthly late interest; after a 30-day formal notice, seizure of assets may follow. Intentional failure exposes the SARL to a 40% bad-faith penalty and criminal enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration update after a share ownership transfer or change in control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the triggering ownership or control change; no annual filing is required if no such change occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-update risks rejection of other RCS filings, administrative penalties, and criminal liability for misleading beneficial-owner declarations under the French Commercial Code.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan Comptable Général, transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; consolidated financial statements of listed groups may apply IFRS as adopted by the European Union.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO confirmation filing. The beneficial-owner declaration is filed at RCS registration and must be updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or share transfer. The SARL must maintain accurate UBO records internally and provide them to judicial or tax authorities upon request; an annual year-end review is best practice to identify any event triggering a filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors' and Managers' Decisions (Registre des décisions des gérants)
Register of Securities Movements (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute Book of General Meetings (Archives des assemblées générales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a threshold-triggered audit; no audit fee applies if the SARL remains below the statutory thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses), accelerated depreciation, and targeted sector incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 May for calendar year-end 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident SARL reports French and foreign-source income; non-residents limited to French-source income
Report only French-source interest and royalties for non-residents

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty €75 per month or 0.75% of tax due (capped at €10,000), plus interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and submit DTA relief claim with supporting documents to tax authority
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0%–5% (treaty-dependent); Interest: 0%–10% (treaty-dependent, often 0% under EU directives)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €10,000,000 local file; €50,000,000 group threshold for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: OECD BEPS Action 5 aligned; holding/IP entities must demonstrate real economic activities with penalties for non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or overstatement of expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to 80% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal restitution, imprisonment, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining entity without substance or economic activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization, loss of tax benefits, and fines up to €10,000+
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax fraud if knowingly involved

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct due diligence or report suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 5% of turnover plus criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length pricing in related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustments, 80% penalties on adjustment, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability if directors approved non-compliant arrangements
